content: Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (the Alliance) is on trial for alleged incitement to subvert state power. Li Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, who pleaded not guilty, concluded 24 days of hearings and received the verdict on Friday, August 21. Chow Hang-tung, former vice-chairwoman of the Alliance, represented herself as a barrister in the case. Without a computer or internet access in prison, she handwrote her submissions, amounting to several hundred pages. At her request, the court played in full two years of candlelight vigils for the June 4th crackdown, recreating the flickering candlelight in Victoria Park and the testimonies of June 4th eyewitnesses. "So I am the last defendant, and also the last vice-chairperson of the first defendant, the Alliance… I am now 41 years old, a barrister, and don't have much of a simple background," Chow Hang-tung said with a smile as she began. Over six days of testimony, she smiled from time to time, but also broke down in tears on several occasions. What do the June 4th vigils and "End one-party dictatorship" mean to Chow Hang-tung? What was her "intention"? This episode of our Podcast continues to take you into the courtroom, using a dramatic reading format to recreate Chow Hang-tung's testimony and the cross-examinations by the judge and the prosecution.
